title: kate-syntax: keep a single case flag
summary: A leading flag group that contains i is already a case flag. translate_pattern does not add a second (?i). A group with only m still gets (?i). The test goes in the existing regex tests module.

lane.reason: A local Qwen3.8 coder model with 27B parameters on the owner Mac codes this packet. The change is one file and stays under about 60 lines.

data_contracts.schema_diff_summary: regex.rs has one test module named tests. Add the new test function at the end of that module, before its closing brace. Do not write a second mod tests. Change only has_leading_case_flag. Keep the let-else on strip_prefix of (? . The flag text is the slice before the next ). Return true when that text contains i. Return that boolean directly. Do not write if flags.contains('i') { true } else { false }. Do not write two if arms that return the same value. Combine them with ||. That is clippy::if_same_then_else. Do not touch translate_pattern, translate_pcre, invert_greed, push_escape, or replace_captures. The existing test minimal_swaps_greedy_quantifiers stays green. Do not rewrite its assertions. The test a_case_flag_after_m_stays_one_flag checks translate_pattern of (?mi)a with insensitive true, minimal false, and no captures. The result is (?mi)a. translate_pattern of (?m)a with the same flags is (?i)(?m)a. Branch from the current tip of main. base_sha records that tip at planning time. If main has moved, use the new tip. Keep the change under about 60 lines. Stay inside this one behavior. Do not add a second case for coherence. Run the full test module named in the commands, not only the new test.

regression_tests.name: regex::tests::a_case_flag_after_m_stays_one_flag
regression_tests.asserts: This test fails on main. (?mi)a with the insensitive flag becomes (?i)(?mi)a. After the change it stays (?mi)a. (?m)a still gains a leading (?i).
